To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the early administration of mexidol, a drug with antioxidant and free-radical scavenger effects, reduces the severity of vertebral and radicular syndromatic manifestations in patients after the surgical removal of a herniated disk.

the administration of emoxipin, a succinic acid derivate, after the microdisectomia of lumbar disk herniations led to the attenuation of neurodystrophy and radicular syndome without significant changes in the severity of pain, psychological maladaptations and disability during 14 weeks.
emoxipin, mexidol and reamberin can reduce the severity of vertebral and neurologic symptoms after the microdisectomy of disk herniations, and mexidol has the most pronounced effects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the rational pharmacotherapy of diskogenic diseases.
the search of new drugs for the treatment of diskogenic radiculopathy.
the possibility of early (during the first two weeks) and effective (during the first 14 weeks) reduction of neurodystrophies in patients with disk herniations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mexidol is the most effective drug in the treatment of disk herniation.

the use of the above mentioned drugs in the early postoperative period after the microdisectomies for the disk herniations leads to the early attenuation and the long-term reduction of the severity of the vertebral/neurological syndromes.
mexidol, emoxipin, and reamberin are effective in the early postoperative period and mexidol has a more prolonged and pronounced efficacy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mexidol, reamberin, and emoxipin are the drugs of choice for the treatment of radicular and neurologic syndromes after disk surgery.

the early administration of mexidol after the microdisectomy of disk herniation can be considered as an effective way to reduce the severity of radicular and neurologic syndromes and to improve patients' quality of life.
the use of 3-hypopyridine and succinate derivates in patients with disk herniations is effective for the reduction of neurodystrophy, radicular syndrom and DS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mexidol is the best drug in the group of 3-hydraxipiridine and succinate acid derivates for the postoperative pain management in patients after the microdisectomia of disk herniations.
the administration of emoxipin, mexidol or reamberin after microdiscectomies is effective in reducing the severity of vertebral/neuralgic syndromes and DS in patients with disk herniations.

the administration of mexidol after the microdisecotomy of disk herniation leads to the reduction of the severity of vertebral and neurologic symptoms and the improvement of patients' functional state during 14 weeks of follow-up.
